name: eye
definition: Cavitated compound organ that consists of the neural retina, lens, cornea and iris and is the sensory apparatus of the visual system.
overrideNote: DM-34: the eye is one record from the optic vesicle at 11.66 hpf; the alias chain names optic vesicle and optic cup; ZFA starts the eye at Prim-5 (24 hpf). Handoff optic_vesicle_cup runs inside the record (16 to 24 hpf); handoff optic_cup_parts seeds retina, lens and retinal pigmented epithelium over 24 to 30 hpf and the eye mesh ends at 30 hpf (geometryEndHpf) while the record continues as their parent. DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf.

events.text: Optic vesicle evaginates from the forebrain keel at the 6 to 7 somite stage.
events.source: Schmitt and Dowling 1994 J Comp Neurol 344:532-542 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7929890/

events.text: Wing shape at 8 to 9 somites; the vesicle bends ventrally at 10 to 12 somites.
events.source: Schmitt and Dowling 1994 J Comp Neurol 344:532-542 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7929890/

events.text: Evagination ends; invagination into the optic cup starts.
Optic cup; the choroid fissure forms at 18 to 20 somites.
events.source: Schmitt and Dowling 1994 J Comp Neurol 344:532-542 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7929890/

events.text: Eyecups well formed; the retinal pigmented epithelium starts to pigment.
Choroid fissure rotated to ventral.
events.source: Schmitt and Dowling 1994 J Comp Neurol 344:532-542 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7929890/

events.text: Lens fibre differentiation 36 to 48 hpf; posterior suture visible.
events.source: Greiling and Clark 2009 Dev Dyn 238:2254-2265 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19504455/

events.text: Focused retinal image; tracking eye movements from 73 hpf.
events.source: Easter and Nicola 1996 Dev Biol 180:646-663 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8954734/

events.text: Adult eye about 2.0 mm across with a lens near 0.9 mm: at 6 months the centre of the lens sits 0.995 mm from the retinal pigment epithelium (SD-OCT).

19 hpf: optic cup diameter 150 um, depth 90 um; choroid fissure forms (research 03b, Schmitt and Dowling 1994); lens vesicle round by 20 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012)
24 hpf: cup 170 um, depth 110 um, lens 63 um (10 percent of the cup volume, Kwan et al. 2012); BG-36
36 hpf: interpolated; fissure rotated to ventral (Schmitt and Dowling 1994)
48 hpf: eye 230 um, lens 80 um; the fissure is closed (research 03b; BG-36)
72 hpf: eye 270 um, lens 90 um (research 03b); 120 hpf: eye 300 um, lens 101 um (Haug et al. 2010)

168, 360, 720 hpf: interpolated between the 120 hpf row and the 4320 hpf row at a near-constant 8 percent of standard length; lens 160 um at 15 dpf (research 03b lens record, Wang et al. 2020); sizeRefSl from growth.standardLengthMm (DM-15)
boundsMarginMm 0.6: the eyes are the widest part of the head in dorsal view and protrude beyond the body-model outline (about 0.1 mm per side at 120 hpf, up to 0.6 mm in the adult); W007 allowance
1080 hpf: eye 0.96 mm, lens 0.38 mm at SL 12 mm, interpolated between the 720 hpf and 4320 hpf rows (estimate)

4320 hpf: eye 2.0 mm at SL 25 mm. Collery et al. 2014 measure 0.995 mm +/- 0.037 mm from the centre of the lens to the retinal pigment epithelium by SD-OCT in 6-month fish (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4205002/), and 4320 hpf is 6 months, so the retinal sphere is about 1.99 mm across. Lens 0.9 mm, about 1 mm in the adult (Bell et al. 2014 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4259836/), which also matches the 1.080 mm ray-traced focal length of Collery et al. 2014 under Matthiessen's ratio. 2160 hpf: eye 1.44 mm, lens 0.6 mm at SL 18 mm (90 dpf), scaled to the same 8 percent of standard length (estimate). Review action 13: the earlier series ran to 2.6 mm at 4320 hpf, which is about 11 percent of standard length and about 30 percent over the measurement.

placement: u 0.10 (BG-36); w 0.5 at 11.66 and 0.55 at 16 hpf while the vesicle is attached to the forebrain (phase 1 review R15), 0.85 from 19 hpf (the eyes sit on the head sides); v 0.15 at 11.66 and 0.1 at 16 hpf keep the vesicle in the dorsal part of the wrapped axis (regime R2, hV 40 to 80 um), v 0 at 19 and -0.1 from 24 hpf (research 03b: the ventral half below the brain floor in the larva)
boundsMarginMm 0.6: the eyes are the widest part of the head in dorsal view and protrude beyond the body-model outline (W007 allowance)

placement u 0.07 from 19 to 36 hpf, 0.075 at 48, 0.085 at 72 and 0.10 from 120 hpf (review R04): Kimmel 1995 Fig. 1 (Prim-5 to Protruding-mouth) shows the eye almost at the anterior margin of the head, with well under half an eye diameter of tissue in front of it until the jaw protrudes; at u 0.1 the snout ran 0.9 eye diameters ahead of the eye at 48 hpf

cup depth 0.85 of the outer diameter from 36 hpf (review R11): the larval and adult eyeball is a near-complete sphere whose pupil is about half its diameter, so the RPE and retina shells reach 150 degrees from the back pole and the eye bulges beyond the head outline in the dorsal view (Kimmel 1995 Fig. 1 dorsal views), as the 0.6-diameter cup of the optic-cup stages (19 to 24 hpf, Kwan et al. 2012) does not; the lens sits in the pupil

Phase 2 visual calibration (RN-02): the cup depth is 0.88 of the outer diameter at 24 hpf and 0.95 from 48 hpf, so the retinal pigment epithelium wraps about 154 degrees of the eyeball and leaves a pupil of about half the eye diameter. The eye then reads as a dark disc with a bright lens in lateral view, as the Kimmel stage series and the painted series show from 24 hpf, instead of an open bowl.

name: retina
definition: Multi-tissue structure that contains the retinal neural layer and the retinal pigmented epithelium, and develops from the optic cup.
overrideNote: Handoff optic_cup_parts: seeded from the eye (optic cup) at the window start 24 hpf (D9, DM-34); ZFA starts the term at Prim-15 (30 hpf). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf. The 2 h fade-in reaches full opacity at 26 hpf, so the eye reads as a dark cup with a pale lens and not as a cyan bullseye (owner painted stage series, 24 hr panel; the handoff window start fixes visibleFromHpf at 24 hpf, E034).

events.text: Presumptive neural retina (inner cup layer) (ZFA, 26+ somites).
Retina term starts (ZFIN, prim-15).
First ganglion cells differentiate ventronasally about 28 to 32 hpf; lamination 48 to 72 hpf (unverified hours).
Most cell classes present in central retina by 72 to 96 hpf; outer segments appear (Easter & Nicola 1996 Dev Biol 180:646-663 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8954734/).
Continuous growth from the ciliary marginal zone throughout life (Marcus et al. 1999 Vis Neurosci 16:417).

name: retinal pigmented epithelium
definition: A monolayer of pigmented epithelium covering the neural retina; develops from the outer of the two layers of the optic cup.
overrideNote: Handoff optic_cup_parts: seeded from the eye (optic cup) at the window start 24 hpf (D9, DM-34); ZFA starts the term at Prim-15 (30 hpf). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf. The 2 h fade-in reaches full pigment at 26 hpf, when melanin is first visible in the animal, so the eye reads as a dark cup and not as a cyan bullseye (owner painted stage series, 24 hr panel; the handoff window start fixes visibleFromHpf at 24 hpf, E034). The earlier 12 h fade was the pigmentation ramp of research 03b (24 to 36 hpf).

events.text: Presumptive RPE (outer cup layer) (ZFA, 26+ somites); PE shrinks as cells move into the neural retina 14 to 24 hpf (Li, Joseph & Easter 2000 Dev Dyn 218:175-188 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10822269/).

Melanin first appears in the retinal pigmented epithelium at prim-5: "Pigment formation begins in cells of the pigmented retinal epithelium and then in melanophores dorsolaterally in the skin" (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html).

RPE term starts at prim-15 (ZFIN). The pigmented eye is visible from prim-5, when "Pigment formation begins in cells of the pigmented retinal epithelium" (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html); how dark it is at prim-15 is an estimate.
RPE fully pigmented (estimate).

name: lens
definition: Portion of tissue that is a transparent, biconvex structure located in the eye through which light is focused.
overrideNote: Handoff optic_cup_parts: seeded from the eye (optic cup) at the window start 24 hpf (D9, DM-34); ZFA starts the term at Prim-15 (30 hpf). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf. The 2 h fade-in reaches full opacity at 26 hpf, so the eye reads as a dark cup with a pale lens and not as a cyan bullseye (owner painted stage series, 24 hr panel; the handoff window start fixes visibleFromHpf at 24 hpf, E034).

events.text: Lens placode (ZFA, 5-9 somites); first visible as a thickening at about 15 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/).
Solid lens vesicle (ZFA, 20-25 somites); round by 20 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/).

Lens pinches off from the ectoderm as a solid cell mass (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/, Dahm et al. 2007 Exp Eye Res 85:74-89 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17467692/).
Lens term starts (ZFIN, prim-15).
Posterior suture visible (Greiling & Clark 2009 Dev Dyn 238:2254-2265 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19504455/).
Lens optically functional; image focused on photoreceptors (Easter & Nicola 1996 Dev Biol 180:646-663 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8954734/).

name: otic placode
definition: Primordium of the ear epithelium before it hollows into the otic vesicle, present beside the hindbrain rudiment in the mid-segmentation period. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for ear by T. Whitfield.)
overrideNote: ZFIN starts the otic placode at Bud (10 hpf) for the specified field; the placode is first visible as an ectodermal thickening at 9 to 14 somites, so the model draws it from 14 hpf (research 03b deviations table; ear.html; Haddon and Lewis 1996). Handoff otic_placode_vesicle: the placode hands off to the otic vesicle over 16 to 18 hpf (D9), so the record ends at 18 hpf; ZFA ends it at 26+ somites (24 hpf).

events.text: Otic placode term starts (ZFIN, bud).

name: otic vesicle
definition: Epithelial sac present beside the fifth rhombomere; forms the semicircular canals dorsally and the otolith organs ventrally, and houses the acoustico-vestibular sensory epithelia (maculae) of hair cells. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for ear by T. Whitfield.)
overrideNote: Handoff otic_placode_vesicle: seeded from the otic placode at the window start 16 hpf (D9), which equals the ZFA start; the 2 h fade-in is the cross-fade. Handoff otic_vesicle_ear: the vesicle hands off to the inner ear over 66 to 72 hpf (D9), so the record ends at 72 hpf with a 6 h fade-out; ZFA end stage Unknown (E008).

events.text: Otic vesicle term starts (ZFA, 14-19 somites).
Lumen forms by cavitation of the otic placode.
events.source: Haddon and Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/

events.text: Two otoliths appear.

events.text: First hair cells in two maculae under the otoliths.

events.text: Endolymphatic sac evaginates from the dorsal wall.
Anterior, lateral and posterior protrusions (canal pillars) start to grow, 42 to 48 hpf.
All three canal pillars fused; the inner ear record takes over (D9 otic_vesicle_ear).

name: inner ear
definition: The auditory (hearing) and vestibular (balance) organ of the fish, equivalent to the inner ear of amniotes. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for ear by T. Whitfield.)
overrideNote: Handoff otic_vesicle_ear: the inner ear is the to record; its ZFA start (20-25 somites, 19 hpf) precedes the window 66 to 72 hpf, so it keeps that start (DM-33, E034) and is drawn from 19 hpf as the endolymph space inside the otic vesicle. DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf.

events.text: Inner ear term starts (ZFIN, 20-25 somites).
Three semicircular canals formed by 3 dpf (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/).
About 80 hair cells per macula between 3 and 7 dpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
Lagenar macula with differentiated hair cells by 15 dpf (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/).
Adult ear about 2.3 mm long with three otoliths (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/, https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html).

19 to 66 hpf: ZFIN starts the inner ear at 20-25 somites (19 hpf), inside the otic vesicle window, and DM-33 keeps that start (E034); the inner ear is the endolymph space inside the otic vesicle epithelium, drawn as 0.8 to 0.85 of the vesicle lumen (the otic vesicle record sizes less two walls; research 03b otic vesicle rows) so the two meshes never coincide; the otoliths sit on its floor (research 03b otolith rows: 5 um at 19.5, 12 um at 24, 25 um at 48 hpf)

66 to 72 hpf: the vesicle fades out (handoff otic_vesicle_ear) and the inner ear grows to the full ear, 180 x 120 x 150 um at 72 hpf (research 03b), width narrowed to 100 um; canals present from 72 hpf with an 80 um loop and a 22 um tube (research 03b semicircular canal row: loop 90, tube 25 um; pillars fused at 72 hpf, Geng et al. 2013); the loops are 10 to 20 percent under the 03b estimates so the dorsolateral canals stay under the elliptical head section
120 hpf: 250 x 170 x 220 um (research 03b, estimate) narrowed to 220 x 110 x 200 um; canal loop 100 um, tube 24 um; otoliths 40 and 55 um (research 03b)

720 hpf: 500 x 350 x 450 um narrowed to 280 wide (research 03b; Bever and Fekete 2002); 2160 hpf: 2300 x 1500 x 2000 um at SL 18 mm (Bever and Fekete 2002 for a 2 year fish) scaled to 1600 x 700 x 1300 um at 90 dpf; canal loop 800 um, tube 120 um; otoliths 450 and 600 um (research 03b adult rows: lapillus 600, sagitta 1000 um, estimate); 4320 hpf: times 1.3 at SL 25 mm

intermediate stages: log-linear in body length (estimate); widths narrowed where the 03b estimate exceeds the body model head (research 03b sizes are estimates; the body-model half-widths hW of src/data/body.json bound them)

placement u 0.22 to 0.21 (BG-37), v 0.2 to 0.1, w 0.75 to 0.47: lateral to the hindbrain, the medial wall against the medulla, the canals under the skin (research 03b spatial note; estimate); the ear moves in and down from 72 hpf as the head section rounds

name: otolith
definition: Portion of organism substance composed of calcium carbonate located in the otolith organ and positioned over a sensory macula; two form in each vesicle during the late segmentation period. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for otolith by T. Whitfield.)

events.text: Otolith term starts at 18 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html); ZFIN start 20-25 somites.

Particles coalesce into two otoliths (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html); two otoliths by 19.5 hpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
Two otoliths easily seen in each vesicle (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Growth by accretion; distinct shapes during the larval period (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html).

Third otolith (asteriscus) forms over the lagena in the second to third week; the atlas draws it from 15 dpf, an estimate. Bever and Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 (PMID 11921341) covers 3 to 30 dpf and has no open-access copy.

sizes.source: research 03b (estimate; scaled from reference images and body length); visible only with Nomarski optics at 19 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html)

name: semicircular canal
definition: Fluid-filled semicircular tubes, arranged orthogonally to each other in the inner ear. Each canal is associated with a crista that detects angular accelerations. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for semicircular canals by T. Whitfield.)
overrideNote: ZFIN starts the semicircular canal at High-pec (42 hpf), when the epithelial projections push into the vesicle; the model draws the canals from 72 hpf, when the three pillars have fused (Geng et al. 2013; research 03b). The inner ear record draws the growing pillars (pillarLengthFraction) from 48 to 72 hpf. DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf.

events.text: Semicircular canal term starts (ZFIN, high-pec).
Epithelial projections push into the vesicle (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/semi_canal/semi.html, Waterman & Bell 1984 Anat Rec 210:101-114 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6486477/).
Lateral projection with anterior and posterior bulges present (Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/).

Anterior and posterior projections fuse with their bulges 57 to 68 hpf (Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/); fusion between long-pec and pec-fin (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/semi_canal/semi.html).
All three pillars fused; canals continue to elongate (Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/).

sizes.source: research 03b (estimate; scaled from reference images and body length); pillars fused at 72 hpf (Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/)

name: olfactory placode
definition: Neurogenic placode that gives rise to the olfactory neurons that which convey odor information to the CNS.
overrideNote: ZFIN starts the olfactory placode at 10-13 somites (14 hpf) for the placodal field; Kimmel first notes the placodes as external thickenings at 26 somites (22 hpf), so the model draws them from 22 hpf (research 03b deviations table; spec DM-20). Handoff olfactory_placode_pit: the placode hands off to the olfactory pit over 22 to 32 hpf (D9), so the record ends at 32 hpf; ZFA ends it at Prim-5 (30 hpf).

events.text: Olfactory field at the anterolateral neural plate edge converges anteriorly (Whitlock & Westerfield 2000 Development 127:3645-3653 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10934010/).
Olfactory placode term starts (ZFIN, 10-13 somites).
The olfactory placodes grow thicker, sitting in front of the forebrain and above it (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Axons grow into the forebrain while epidermis still covers the placode (Hansen & Zeiske 1993 J Comp Neurol 333:289-300 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8345108/).
Placode term ends (ZFIN, prim-5); pit opens.

sizes.source: research 03b (estimate; scaled from reference images and body length); placodes thickened at 22 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html)

name: olfactory pit
definition: Depression on the snout that opens from the olfactory placode and holds the olfactory epithelium; it becomes the nasal cavity with an incurrent and an excurrent nostril in the adult. (ZFA has no definition text for this term; research 03b wording.)
overrideNote: Handoff olfactory_placode_pit: seeded from the olfactory placode at the window start 22 hpf (D9, DM-20); ZFA starts the pit at Prim-15 (30 hpf). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf.

events.text: Olfactory pit term starts (ZFIN, prim-15).
Pit opens as the epidermis separates (Hansen & Zeiske 1993 J Comp Neurol 333:289-300 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8345108/; hour unverified).
Olfactory rod cells present in pits from 36 hpf, consistently beyond 46 hpf (unverified secondary).
Nasal cavity with incurrent and excurrent nostrils (Hansen & Zeiske 1993 J Comp Neurol 333:289-300 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8345108/).

name: posterior lateral line primordium
definition: A migrating group of cells originating from the posterior lateral line placode. The primordium deposits seven to nine neuromasts and interneuromasts between them during its posterior migration to the tail.
overrideNote: ZFA ends the posterior lateral line primordium at Day 4 (120 hpf); the primary primordium has reached the tail by 42 hpf and dissolves into the terminal neuromasts, so the model ends the record at 48 hpf (research 03b events; Dalle Nogare et al. 2020). The secondary primordium is a separate ZFA term (ZFA:0005116) that is not modelled.

events.text: Primordium first visible (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/lat_line/lat_line.html); ZFIN start 20-25 somites (19 hpf).
Migration begins; speed about 100 um/h or 1.7 myotomes/h (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar.html).
Leading edge over myotome 5; first neuromast deposited (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html).

Primary primordium reaches the tail tip and forms the terminal neuromasts (Dalle Nogare et al. 2020 eLife 9:e58251 https://elifesciences.org/articles/58251; ZFIN 50 hpf https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/lat_line/lat_line.html).
Secondary primordium (primII) starts migrating (ZFA, long-pec).
Primordium term ends (ZFIN, day 4).

sizes.source: research 03b; about 100 cells (Pinto-Teixeira et al. 2013 Front Neuroanat 7:33 https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroanatomy/articles/10.3389/fnana.2013.00033/full); 100 to 150 cells (Dalle Nogare et al. 2020 eLife 9:e58251 https://elifesciences.org/articles/58251); dimensions estimate

22 to 36 hpf: the leading edge lies over myotome 3 at 22, 5 at 24, 15 at 30 and 25 at 36 hpf (research 03b position note, Kimmel prim stages): u 0.29, 0.33, 0.56, 0.79 are the somite-array positions of src/data/structures/axial.json (somite k centre at 0.25 + (k - 0.5) x 0.024 at 24 hpf) less half the primordium length; speed about 100 um per hour (phar.html)

name: neuromast
definition: Volcano-shaped lateral line sensory organ located in characteristic positions within the skin epithelium and containing hair cells and their support elements. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.)

events.text: Protoneuromast forms in the trailing primordium (ZFA, 26+ somites).
Neuromast term starts (ZFIN, prim-5).
Hair cells with kinocilia and cupulae; mechanosensitive.
Mature size reached (Pinto-Teixeira et al. 2013 Front Neuroanat 7:33 https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroanatomy/articles/10.3389/fnana.2013.00033/full).

24 to 48 hpf: the primary primordium deposits L1 to L5 plus the terminal neuromasts, one every 5 somites (0.105 u), from u 0.39 to 0.93 (research 03b posterior lateral line: 7 neuromasts at 48 hpf; ZFA primordium definition: seven to nine); count(t) = (primordium u - 0.34) / 0.105 - 0.3 and uEnd = 0.34 + count x 0.105, so deposited neuromasts keep their place while the count grows (segmentArray rule BG-32, BG-42)

72 to 120 hpf: the secondary primordium adds intercalary neuromasts, about 11 to 12 in the posterior line by 4 to 5 dpf (research 03b, lat_line.html); the array count rises to 12 over the same range, so the spacing halves

sizes: diameter 20 um and height 12 um at 24 hpf, 30 x 15 um at 48, 50 x 20 um at 120 hpf (Pinto-Teixeira et al. 2013), 60 x 25 um in the adult (research 03b, estimate): radiiMm along u, v (the disc) and w (the dome height on the skin)
template placement v 0, w 1, mirror: flattened domes on the skin over the horizontal myoseptum, both sides; boundsMarginMm 0.05 for the half dome outside the skin (the neuromast exception of W007)
